chapters.title: The Fear of the LORD Is the Beginning of Knowledge
chapters.html:
Proverbs 1

1The proverbs of Solomon son of David, king of Israel:

2for knowing wisdom and discipline,
for understanding words of insight,

3for receiving the discipline of wise dealing,
righteousness, justice and equity;

4to give shrewdness to the simple,
knowledge and discretion to the young —

5let the wise hear and increase in learning,
and the one who understands gain guidance —

6to understand a proverb and a figure,
the words of the wise and their riddles.

7The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge;
fools despise wisdom and discipline.

8Hear, my son, your father's discipline,
and do not forsake your mother's teaching;

9for they are a graceful garland for your head
and pendants for your neck.

10My son, if sinners entice you,
do not consent.

11If they say, "Come with us;
let us lie in wait for blood;
let us ambush the innocent without cause;

12let us swallow them alive like Sheol,
whole, like those who go down to the pit;

13we will find all kinds of precious wealth;
we will fill our houses with plunder;

14cast your lot among us;
we will all have one purse" —

15my son, do not walk in the way with them;
hold back your foot from their path,

16for their feet run to evil,
and they hurry to shed blood.

17For in vain is a net spread
in the sight of any bird;

18but these men lie in wait for their own blood;
they ambush their own lives.

19Such are the ways of everyone who is greedy for gain;
it takes away the life of its owners.

20Wisdom cries aloud in the street;
in the squares she raises her voice;

21at the head of the noisy streets she calls out;
at the entrances of the city gates she speaks her words:

22"How long, you simple ones, will you love being simple?
How long will scoffers delight in their scoffing
and fools hate knowledge?

23Turn back at my reproof;
I will pour out my spirit to you;
I will make my words known to you.

24Because I called and you refused,
I stretched out my hand and no one paid attention,

25because you ignored all my counsel
and would have none of my reproof,

26I also will laugh at your calamity;
I will mock when terror comes on you,

27when terror comes on you like a storm
and your calamity comes like a whirlwind,
when distress and anguish come upon you.

28Then they will call on me, but I will not answer;
they will seek me diligently but will not find me,

29because they hated knowledge
and did not choose the fear of the LORD,

30would have none of my counsel,
and despised all my reproof.

31So they will eat the fruit of their way
and be filled with their own schemes.

32For the turning away of the simple will kill them,
and the complacency of fools will destroy them;

33but whoever listens to me will dwell secure
and be at ease, without dread of evil."

Notes

  • v1 "The proverbs of Solomon" — mishlei, sayings that compare one thing with another; the title of the whole book (1 Kings 4:32, he spoke three thousand proverbs). In the Ethiopian Bible, Proverbs is chapters 1–24; chapters 25–31 form the book called Reproof (Tegsat).

  • vv2–6 and the words for wisdom — each keeps one English word through the book: chokhmah "wisdom," musar "discipline," binah "understanding" or "insight," da'at "knowledge," ormah "shrewdness," mezimmah "discretion," peti "simple," lets "scoffer." Two words are both "fool": evil (v7), the morally foolish, and kesil (v22), the dull and stubborn.

  • v7 "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge" — the motto of the book; 9:10 and Psalm 111:10 have "wisdom."

  • v8 "your mother's teaching" — torah, "law" when it is God's (Psalm 119), here a parent's teaching in the home.

  • v12 "whole" — temimim, elsewhere "blameless" in this rendering; here, set beside "alive," it means whole, swallowed entire.

  • vv17–18 "in vain is a net spread in the sight of any bird" — a bird that sees the net avoids it; these men walk into their own trap with their eyes open.

  • vv20–33 — Wisdom speaks as a woman in the public square, like a prophet calling the city to turn (Jeremiah 7:13; Isaiah 65:12).

  • v23 "I will pour out my spirit to you" — Wisdom's own spirit, lowercase; compare Joel 2:28, where it is God's.

  • v27 "like a storm" — the read form; the written form is a spelling variant.

chapters.title: If You Seek It Like Silver
chapters.html:
Proverbs 2

1My son, if you receive my words
and treasure up my commandments with you,

2making your ear attentive to wisdom
and inclining your heart to understanding;

3yes, if you call out for insight
and raise your voice for understanding,

4if you seek it like silver
and search for it as for hidden treasures,

5then you will understand the fear of the LORD
and find the knowledge of God.

6For the LORD gives wisdom;
from His mouth come knowledge and understanding.

7He stores up sound wisdom for the upright;
He is a shield to those who walk in integrity,

8guarding the paths of justice
and watching over the way of His faithful ones.

9Then you will understand righteousness and justice
and equity, every good path;

10for wisdom will come into your heart,
and knowledge will be pleasant to your soul;

11discretion will watch over you;
understanding will guard you,

12to deliver you from the way of evil,
from men who speak perverse things,

13who forsake the paths of uprightness
to walk in the ways of darkness,

14who rejoice in doing evil
and delight in the perversity of evil,

15whose paths are crooked
and who are devious in their ways.

16It will deliver you from the strange woman,
from the foreign woman with her smooth words,

17who forsakes the companion of her youth
and forgets the covenant of her God;

18for her house sinks down to death,
and her paths to the shades;

19none who go to her come back,
nor do they reach the paths of life.

20So you will walk in the way of the good
and keep to the paths of the righteous.

21For the upright will dwell in the land,
and the blameless will remain in it;

22but the wicked will be cut off from the land,
and the treacherous will be uprooted from it.

Notes

  • vv1–4 "if… if… if" — one long sentence: the seeking is the son's, and the gift is God's (v6).

  • v7 "He stores up" — the read form; the written form has "and He stored up." "Sound wisdom" is tushiyyah, practical skill that succeeds.

  • v8 "His faithful ones" — the read form, plural; the written form is singular. Chasid, as in the Psalms.

  • v16 "the strange woman… the foreign woman" — zarah and nokhriyyah: another man's wife, outside the bounds of the marriage covenant, the figure of chapters 5–7.

  • v17 "the covenant of her God" — marriage as a covenant made before God (Malachi 2:14).

  • v18 "the shades" — refa'im, the dead (Psalm 88:10).

  • vv21–22 — the land kept by the upright and lost by the wicked, as in Psalm 37:9–11, 29.

chapters.title: Trust in the LORD with All Your Heart
chapters.html:
Proverbs 3

1My son, do not forget my teaching,
but let your heart keep my commandments,

2for length of days and years of life
and peace they will add to you.

3Do not let loyal love and truth forsake you;
bind them around your neck;
write them on the tablet of your heart.

4So you will find favor and good understanding
in the sight of God and man.

5Trust in the LORD with all your heart,
and do not lean on your own understanding.

6In all your ways acknowledge Him,
and He will make your paths straight.

7Do not be wise in your own eyes;
fear the LORD and turn away from evil.

8It will be healing to your navel
and refreshment to your bones.

9Honor the LORD with your wealth
and with the firstfruits of all your produce;

10then your barns will be filled with plenty,
and your vats will burst with new wine.

11My son, do not reject the discipline of the LORD,
and do not resent His reproof,

12for the LORD reproves the one He loves,
as a father the son in whom he delights.

13Blessed is the one who finds wisdom,
and the one who gains understanding,

14for her profit is better than profit from silver,
and her yield than fine gold.

15She is more precious than jewels,
and nothing you desire can compare with her.

16Long life is in her right hand;
in her left hand are riches and honor.

17Her ways are ways of pleasantness,
and all her paths are peace.

18She is a tree of life to those who take hold of her,
and those who hold her fast are called blessed.

19The LORD by wisdom founded the earth;
by understanding He established the heavens;

20by His knowledge the deeps broke open,
and the clouds drop down the dew.

21My son, do not let them slip from your sight;
keep sound wisdom and discretion,

22and they will be life for your soul
and grace for your neck.

23Then you will walk your way in safety,
and your foot will not stumble.

24When you lie down, you will not be afraid;
when you lie down, your sleep will be sweet.

25Do not be afraid of sudden terror
or of the ruin of the wicked when it comes,

26for the LORD will be your confidence
and will keep your foot from being caught.

27Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due,
when it is in your power to do it.

28Do not say to your neighbor, "Go, and come back;
tomorrow I will give it" —
when you have it with you.

29Do not plot harm against your neighbor,
who lives trustingly beside you.

30Do not quarrel with anyone without cause,
when he has done you no harm.

31Do not envy a man of violence,
and do not choose any of his ways,

32for the devious person is detestable to the LORD,
but His confidence is with the upright.

33The LORD's curse is on the house of the wicked,
but He blesses the dwelling of the righteous.

34Toward the scoffers He is scornful,
but to the humble He gives grace.

35The wise will inherit honor,
but fools carry away disgrace.

Notes

  • v3 "loyal love and truth… write them on the tablet of your heart" — chesed and emet, as in Exodus 34:6; the tablet as in Jeremiah 31:33.

  • v8 "healing to your navel" — shor, the navel or the cord; the Greek reads "your body."

  • v11 "do not resent His reproof" — qots, to dread or recoil from; "loathe" is kept in this rendering for sheqets.

  • vv11–12 — Hebrews 12:5–6 quotes these lines from the Greek, which reads the last line "and He scourges every son whom He receives."

  • v15 "more precious than jewels" — peninim, perhaps corals or pearls; the read form is a spelling variant.

  • v18 "a tree of life" — as in Genesis 2:9 and 3:22; wisdom gives what was lost (Revelation 22:2).

  • vv19–20 — the same wisdom by which God made the world, as in 8:22–31 and Psalm 104:24.

  • vv27–28 — "to whom it is due" and "your neighbor" are the read forms; the written forms are spelling variants.

  • v34 "to the humble He gives grace" — the read form anavim, "humble"; the written form aniyyim, "afflicted." James 4:6 and 1 Peter 5:5 quote the Greek: God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.

chapters.title: Keep Your Heart
chapters.html:
Proverbs 4

1Hear, sons, a father's discipline,
and pay attention, so that you may know understanding,

2for I give you good learning;
do not forsake my teaching.

3When I was a son to my father,
tender, the only one in the sight of my mother,

4he taught me and said to me,
"Let your heart hold fast my words;
keep my commandments and live.

5Get wisdom; get understanding;
do not forget, and do not turn away from the words of my mouth.

6Do not forsake her, and she will keep you;
love her, and she will guard you.

7The beginning of wisdom is this: get wisdom,
and with all you have gotten, get understanding.

8Prize her highly, and she will exalt you;
she will honor you if you embrace her.

9She will place on your head a graceful garland;
she will give you a crown of beauty."

10Hear, my son, and accept my words,
and the years of your life will be many.

11I have taught you the way of wisdom;
I have led you in paths of uprightness.

12When you walk, your step will not be hampered,
and if you run, you will not stumble.

13Keep hold of discipline; do not let go;
guard her, for she is your life.

14Do not enter the path of the wicked,
and do not walk in the way of evil men.

15Avoid it; do not go on it;
turn away from it and pass on.

16For they cannot sleep unless they have done evil;
they are robbed of sleep unless they have made someone stumble.

17For they eat the bread of wickedness
and drink the wine of violence.

18But the path of the righteous is like the light of dawn,
which shines brighter and brighter until full day.

19The way of the wicked is like deep darkness;
they do not know what makes them stumble.

20My son, pay attention to my words;
incline your ear to my sayings.

21Do not let them slip from your sight;
keep them within your heart.

22For they are life to those who find them,
and healing to all their flesh.

23Above all that you guard, keep your heart,
for from it flow the springs of life.

24Put away from you crooked speech,
and put devious lips far from you.

25Let your eyes look straight ahead,
and your gaze be fixed straight before you.

26Make level the path of your feet,
and all your ways will be sure.

27Do not turn to the right or to the left;
turn your foot away from evil.

Notes

  • vv3–9 — the father passes on what his own father taught him: three generations of the same teaching.

  • v3 "the only one in the sight of my mother" — yachid, an only or beloved son; Solomon was the son David and Bathsheba kept (2 Samuel 12:24).

  • v7 "The beginning of wisdom is this: get wisdom" — the first step is the decision to seek it, whatever it costs; the Greek leaves out the verse.

  • v16 "unless they have made someone stumble" — the read form; the written form is a spelling variant.

  • v18 "like the light of dawn, which shines brighter and brighter" — the righteous grow in light; the wicked walk in darkness and do not even see what trips them (v19).

  • v20 "my sayings" — amarai, the plural of imrah; here the father's spoken words.

  • v23 "Above all that you guard, keep your heart" — the heart, the seat of thought and will, from which life flows (Matthew 15:18–19).

chapters.title: Drink Water from Your Own Cistern
chapters.html:
Proverbs 5

1My son, pay attention to my wisdom;
incline your ear to my understanding,

2so that you may keep discretion
and your lips may guard knowledge.

3For the lips of the strange woman drip honey,
and her mouth is smoother than oil;

4but in the end she is bitter as wormwood,
sharp as a two-edged sword.

5Her feet go down to death;
her steps take hold of Sheol.

6She does not consider the path of life;
her ways wander, and she does not know it.

7Now then, sons, listen to me,
and do not turn away from the words of my mouth.

8Keep your way far from her,
and do not go near the door of her house,

9or you will give your vigor to others
and your years to the merciless,

10or strangers will take their fill of your strength,
and your labors will go to the house of a foreigner,

11and at the end of your life you will groan,
when your flesh and body are consumed,

12and you will say, "How I hated discipline,
and my heart despised reproof!

13I did not listen to the voice of my teachers
or incline my ear to my instructors.

14I was almost in utter ruin
in the assembly and congregation."

15Drink water from your own cistern,
flowing water from your own well.

16Should your springs be scattered abroad,
streams of water in the streets?

17Let them be yours alone,
and not for strangers with you.

18Let your fountain be blessed,
and rejoice in the wife of your youth,

19a loving doe, a graceful mountain goat.
Let her breasts satisfy you at all times;
be captivated always by her love.

20Why, my son, should you be captivated by a strange woman
and embrace the bosom of a foreigner?

21For a man's ways are before the eyes of the LORD,
and He weighs all his paths.

22The iniquities of the wicked man ensnare him,
and he is held fast in the cords of his sin.

23He dies for lack of discipline,
and in the greatness of his folly he goes astray.

Notes

  • v3 "the strange woman" — zarah, as in 2:16, another man's wife.

  • v6 "She does not consider the path of life" — pen, often "lest," here "so that she does not": she never stops to weigh her way.

  • vv9–10 "or you will give… or strangers will take" — pen, "or else": adultery costs strength, years and wealth.

  • v14 "in the assembly and congregation" — exposed and judged before the whole community (Deuteronomy 22:22).

  • vv15–18 "cistern… well… springs… fountain" — the wife as the man's own well of water (Song of Songs 4:12, 15); v16 can be read as a question or as a statement of a blessing that spreads to children.

  • vv19, 20, 23 "be captivated… be captivated… goes astray" — the same verb, shagah, three times: be lost in your wife's love, not in a stranger's, or you will be lost in your folly.

  • v21 "He weighs all his paths" — or "levels"; God sees and measures every way.

chapters.title: Go to the Ant, You Sluggard
chapters.html:
Proverbs 6

1My son, if you have become surety for your neighbor,
have given your pledge for a stranger,

2you are snared by the words of your mouth,
caught by the words of your mouth.

3Do this, then, my son, and save yourself,
since you have come into your neighbor's hand:
go, humble yourself, and press your neighbor hard.

4Give no sleep to your eyes
or slumber to your eyelids;

5save yourself like a gazelle from the hunter's hand,
like a bird from the hand of the fowler.

6Go to the ant, you sluggard;
consider her ways and be wise.

7She has no chief,
officer or ruler,

8yet she prepares her bread in summer
and gathers her food at harvest.

9How long will you lie there, sluggard?
When will you rise from your sleep?

10A little sleep, a little slumber,
a little folding of the hands to rest,

11and your poverty will come on you like a prowler,
and your want like an armed man.

12A worthless person, a wicked man,
goes about with crooked speech,

13winks with his eyes, signals with his feet,
points with his fingers,

14with perversity in his heart devises evil continually,
sowing discord.

15So calamity will come on him suddenly;
in an instant he will be broken beyond healing.

16There are six things the LORD hates,
seven that are detestable to Him:

17haughty eyes, a lying tongue,
and hands that shed innocent blood,

18a heart that devises wicked plans,
feet that hurry to run to evil,

19a false witness who breathes out lies,
and one who sows discord among brothers.

20My son, keep your father's commandment,
and do not forsake your mother's teaching.

21Bind them on your heart always;
tie them around your neck.

22When you walk, it will lead you;
when you lie down, it will watch over you;
and when you awake, it will talk with you.

23For the commandment is a lamp and the teaching a light,
and the reproofs of discipline are the way of life,

24to keep you from the evil woman,
from the smooth tongue of the foreign woman.

25Do not desire her beauty in your heart,
and do not let her capture you with her eyelashes;

26for a prostitute costs only a loaf of bread,
but another man's wife hunts for a precious life.

27Can a man carry fire in his lap
and his clothes not be burned?

28Or can a man walk on hot coals
and his feet not be scorched?

29So is he who goes in to his neighbor's wife;
none who touches her will go unpunished.

30People do not despise a thief if he steals
to satisfy his hunger when he is hungry;

31yet if he is caught, he will pay sevenfold;
he will give all the goods of his house.

32He who commits adultery with a woman lacks sense;
he who does it destroys himself.

33He will get wounds and disgrace,
and his reproach will not be wiped away.

34For jealousy makes a man furious,
and he will not spare in the day of vengeance.

35He will accept no compensation;
he will refuse, though you multiply gifts.

Notes

  • v1 "if you have become surety" — guaranteeing another's debt with a handshake (taqa kaf, "struck hands"); the book warns against it again (11:15; 17:18; 22:26–27).

  • v6 "Go to the ant, you sluggard" — atsel, the lazy man, a figure the book returns to (24:30–34 repeats vv10–11).

  • v14 "sowing discord" — the read form midyanim; the written form is a spelling variant.

  • v16 "six things… seven" — the numerical saying, the last item the one that matters most (30:15–31; Amos 1:3). "Detestable" is to'evah; the read form is singular.

  • v23 "the commandment is a lamp and the teaching a light" — as in Psalm 119:105.

  • v26 "a prostitute costs only a loaf of bread" — the Hebrew is terse, "for a prostitute — to a loaf of bread"; the cost of the one is small, of the other a life.

  • v32 "lacks sense" — chasar lev, literally "lacks heart," the heart as the seat of understanding.

  • vv34–35 — the wronged husband's jealousy, which no payment will buy off; the thief can repay (v31), the adulterer cannot.

chapters.title: Her House Is the Way to Sheol
chapters.html:
Proverbs 7

1My son, keep my words
and treasure up my commandments with you.

2Keep my commandments and live;
keep my teaching as the apple of your eye.

3Bind them on your fingers;
write them on the tablet of your heart.

4Say to wisdom, "You are my sister,"
and call understanding your close relative,

5to keep you from the strange woman,
from the foreign woman with her smooth words.

6For at the window of my house
I looked out through my lattice,

7and I saw among the simple,
I noticed among the youths,
a young man lacking sense,

8passing along the street near her corner,
taking the road to her house

9in the twilight, in the evening of the day,
in the black of night and the darkness.

10Then a woman comes to meet him,
dressed as a prostitute, with a guarded heart.

11She is loud and unruly;
her feet do not stay at home;

12now in the street, now in the squares,
and at every corner she lies in wait.

13She seizes him and kisses him,
and with a brazen face she says to him,

14"I had peace offerings to make;
today I have paid my vows.

15So I came out to meet you,
to seek your face eagerly, and I have found you.

16I have spread my bed with coverings,
colored linens from Egypt.

17I have sprinkled my bed
with myrrh, aloes and cinnamon.

18Come, let us drink our fill of love until morning;
let us delight ourselves with caresses.

19For the man is not at home;
he has gone on a long journey.

20He took a bag of money with him;
he will come home at the full moon."

21With her many persuasions she turns him aside;
with her smooth lips she compels him.

22All at once he follows her,
as an ox goes to the slaughter,
or as a fool to the stocks for discipline,

23until an arrow pierces his liver —
as a bird rushes into a snare;
he does not know it will cost him his life.

24Now then, sons, listen to me,
and pay attention to the words of my mouth.

25Do not let your heart turn aside to her ways;
do not stray into her paths;

26for many are the victims she has brought down,
and numerous are all whom she has slain.

27Her house is the way to Sheol,
going down to the chambers of death.

Notes

  • v2 "as the apple of your eye" — ishon, "the little man" of the eye, the pupil, as in Deuteronomy 32:10 and Psalm 17:8.

  • v5 — the same words as 2:16, and the English there is followed.

  • v9 "in the black of night" — be'ishon laylah, "in the pupil of the night," the same word as v2: the darkest point.

  • v14 "I had peace offerings to make; today I have paid my vows" — the meat of a peace offering had to be eaten within a day or two (Leviticus 7:16); she has a feast at home and an empty house.

  • v19 "For the man is not at home" — she does not say "my husband," only "the man."

  • v22 "or as a fool to the stocks for discipline" — the Hebrew is obscure, ukhe'ekhes el musar evil; ekhes is an anklet or fetter (Isaiah 3:18). The Greek reads "as a dog to bonds."

  • vv26–27 — the end of the young man of v7, and the end of the warning that began in 2:16–19.

chapters.title: Wisdom Calls
chapters.html:
Proverbs 8

1Does not wisdom call,
and understanding raise her voice?

2On the top of the heights beside the way,
where the paths meet, she takes her stand;

3beside the gates at the entrance of the city,
at the entry of the doors, she cries aloud:

4"To you, men, I call,
and my voice is to the children of man.

5You simple ones, learn shrewdness;
you fools, learn sense.

6Listen, for I speak noble things,
and from the opening of my lips come right things,

7for my mouth utters truth;
wickedness is detestable to my lips.

8All the words of my mouth are in righteousness;
there is nothing twisted or crooked in them.

9They are all straight to the one who understands,
and right to those who find knowledge.

10Take my discipline instead of silver,
and knowledge rather than choice gold,

11for wisdom is better than jewels,
and nothing desirable can compare with her.

12I, wisdom, dwell with shrewdness,
and I find knowledge and discretion.

13The fear of the LORD is to hate evil.
Pride and arrogance and the way of evil
and the perverse mouth I hate.

14Counsel and sound wisdom are mine;
I am understanding; strength is mine.

15By me kings reign,
and rulers decree what is just;

16by me princes rule,
and nobles, all who judge rightly.

17I love those who love me,
and those who seek me diligently find me.

18Riches and honor are with me,
enduring wealth and righteousness.

19My fruit is better than gold, even fine gold,
and my yield than choice silver.

20I walk in the way of righteousness,
in the paths of justice,

21granting wealth to those who love me
and filling their treasuries.

22The LORD got me at the beginning of His way,
before His works of old.

23From everlasting I was set up,
from the beginning, before the earth was.

24When there were no deeps I was brought forth,
when there were no springs heavy with water.

25Before the mountains had been settled,
before the hills, I was brought forth,

26before He had made the earth or the fields
or the first of the dust of the world.

27When He established the heavens, I was there;
when He drew a circle on the face of the deep,

28when He made firm the skies above,
when the springs of the deep grew strong,

29when He assigned to the sea its limit,
so that the waters would not pass beyond His command,
when He marked out the foundations of the earth,

30then I was beside Him as a master workman,
and I was His delight day by day,
rejoicing before Him always,

31rejoicing in His inhabited world
and delighting in the children of man.

32Now then, sons, listen to me:
blessed are those who keep my ways.

33Hear discipline and be wise,
and do not ignore it.

34Blessed is the one who listens to me,
watching daily at my gates,
waiting beside my doorposts.

35For whoever finds me finds life
and obtains favor from the LORD;

36but whoever misses me harms his own soul;
all who hate me love death."

Notes

  • vv1–3 — Wisdom calls again in the open places, as in 1:20–21, now not in rebuke but in invitation.

  • v11 — nearly the same as 3:15; here "nothing desirable" (chafatsim) for "nothing you desire."

  • v16 "all who judge rightly" — many Hebrew manuscripts and the Greek read "all the judges of the earth."

  • v17 "I love those who love me" — the read form; the written form has "those who love her."

  • v22 "The LORD got me" — qanani, the verb of Genesis 4:1, I have gotten a man, and 14:19, getter of heaven and earth. It can mean acquire, possess, or bring into being; the Greek reads "created me," and the early church argued over the verse. The New Testament speaks of Christ in these terms: the firstborn of all creation… in Him all things were created (Colossians 1:15–17; John 1:1–3).

  • v23 "I was set up" — nissakhti, the verb of Psalm 2:6, I have set My king; some read "I was woven."

  • v30 "as a master workman" — amon; others read amun, "as a little child," or "faithfully." Either way Wisdom was with God at creation, delighting.

  • v36 "whoever misses me" — chote'i, "whoever sins against me," the root meaning "to miss the mark."
